transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It actually sounds like your washer-dryer might be behaving normally. Most condenser washer-dryers use a small trickle of cold water during the drying cycle to cool down the hot air and condense the moisture from your clothes into liquid water, which is then pumped away. If you hear water running in and out, it is likely this condensation process. However, we need to rule out a blockage that might be causing excess water to build up or leak. Could you please check the pump filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) and tell me if it was full of fluff or debris? Also, is there any water leaking from the machine onto the floor while it runs?
Thank you. No leaks on the floor at all. I haven't checked the pump filter, though - the machine is only two months old, so is that really necessary if nothing is actually going wrong?

It is not strictly necessary to check the filter if there are no leaks and the machine seems to be working correctly. You can leave it as is. If you ever find clothes are not drying well or the machine takes much longer than usual, then checking the filter and ensuring the load isn't too large would be the next steps.

candidates: Normal condensation process (water intake for cooling) (high)
Blocked pump filter or drain path causing water to recirculate/leak (medium)
Faulty valve or sensor letting in too much water (low)
